chapter: Louis Armstrong, Gene Krupa and the drum school
title: Armstrong's band chemistry

story.theme_name: Working with and around Louis Armstrong
story.community_name: Playing with and around Louis Armstrong

blocks.x: So I take it you enjoyed playing with that band.
That was one of the highlights of my whole career, working with Louie, in that band, in that particular band.

Great, I never seen an argument or anything in there. Great, everybody. Well see, that's the way Louie would hire you. Of course your character first and he'd have to like your playing, but Louie with that personality that he had, he didn't want anybody to be in there that's going to be a drag. He wants everybody in there to get along, because he's going to get along, and that's his personality and he just isn't going to put up with anybody that's going to be a drag in there, you know. Because he's not going around trying to reprimand anybody, because that just isn't his personality. He's just always feeling good, you know, and he want to play. In order to play like Louie you've got to feel happy ninety percent of the time.
How often was it that he would really play as opposed to kind of coasting?

Oh goodness, I'd say Louie played about 80 percent of the time, really played. Twenty percent of the time, sometimes you know his chops would be down or it's all according to how long the jump was. But 80 percent of the time Louie's chops were always good. He used to inspire us some time. We were all together about five years. Some nights, man, it used to be incredible the way that Louie would play up there.
